abstract: For any simple graph $G$ of order $n$, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j(G)x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for $j\ge1$ and $x^{\langle 0\rangle}=1.$ Brenti (1992) introduced the $\tau$-polynomial of $G$ and its augmented version, defined by $$\tau(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^n c_j(G)x^j~~~\text{and}~~~\overline \tau(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^n j!c_j(G)x^j.$$ He asked whether $\tau(G,x)$ is always real-rooted and whether the coefficient sequence of $\overline \tau(G,x)$ is always log-concave. In this paper, we prove that for every integer $d\ge4$, there exists an integer $h_d\ge3$ such that $c_2(G)^2<c_1(G)c_3(G)$ for every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $h_d$. For such graphs, the coefficient sequences of both polynomials fail log-concavity at $j=2$, and thus both polynomials have nonreal roots by Newton's inequalities. This gives counterexamples to both questions among connected regular graphs of arbitrarily large girth.
hook: Graphs with large girth disprove Brenti's questions on real roots and log-concavity.
summary: Brenti asked whether the tau-polynomial of a graph always has only real roots and whether a related coefficient sequence is log-concave. The authors prove that regular graphs of degree at least 4 and large enough girth break log-concavity at j=2, answering both questions negatively. The counterexamples are existence results for large girth, not small explicit graphs.
title: Non-log-concave $\tau$-polynomials of regular graphs
